question: Who was sworn in as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on 14 May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Bhushan Ramakrishna Gavai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Justice Bhushan Ramakrishna Gavai was sworn in as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on **14 May 2025**.
 
• He succeeded Justice Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud, who served as the 50th Chief Justice of India.
 
• Justice Gavai is known for his landmark judgments and his significant contributions to the Indian judiciary.
 
• He previously served as a judge in the Supreme Court of India, appointed on **24 May 2019**.
 
• Justice Gavai's tenure as Chief Justice is expected to uphold judicial integrity and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI)**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary system and the Supreme Court, the highest judicial forum in India.
 
• The appointment of the CJI is made by the President of India based on seniority among Supreme Court judges.
 
• The CJI plays a crucial role in judicial reforms, constitutional interpretation, and handling cases of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India**
 
 
• The Supreme Court was established on January 28, 1950, and is located in New Delhi.
 
• It is the guardian of the Constitution and has the power of judicial review.
 
• The Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice and a maximum of 33 other judges.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Appointments in India**
 
 
• Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India under Article 124 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The process involves consultation with senior judges and follows the principle of seniority.
 
 
 
• **Tenure of the Chief Justice of India**
 
 
• The tenure of the CJI depends on the age of retirement, which is fixed at 65 years for Supreme Court judges.
 
• The CJI's role includes presiding over court proceedings and administrative responsibilities of the judiciary.
